solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Brief press about fool blocking state (7)

indicators.note: a brief word is cut short, so IMPEL loses its last letter
about means around, so the shortened press is placed around the fool

annotation.surface: A curt newspaper is having a go at some idiot who is obstructing the government.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Blocking' seems to go with 'fool', as if the fool were the one doing the blocking, but it belongs with 'state' as the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: An impasse is a deadlock, a state in which progress is blocked.

entries.clue: Popular drink, by turns mild and short on taste (7)

indicators.note: take every other letter of mild

blocks.note: the alternate letters of mILD are I and D

annotation.surface: A popular drink is sometimes mild and a bit lacking in flavour.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Mild' reads like a tasting note beside 'short on taste', but it only supplies its second and fourth letters.
annotation.definitionFit: Something insipid lacks flavour, is short on taste.

entries.clue: Savoury casserole with stewed apricots (6,5)

indicators.note: the apricots are cooked into a new arrangement

blocks.note: a pot is a casserole dish

annotation.surface: A recipe for a savoury casserole made with stewed apricots.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Savoury' is a noun, a salty snack, not an adjective describing the casserole; a potato crisp is what Americans call a potato chip.
annotation.definitionFit: A crisp is a savoury snack, as opposed to a sweet.

entries.clue: Give advance payment to authorise rent from tenant? (6)

blocks.note: to sub someone is to advance them money

annotation.surface: Pay a deposit to approve a tenant's rent.
annotation.walkthrough: To sub someone is British slang for lending them money ahead of payday.
annotation.definitionFit: To sublet is to rent a property from someone who is themselves a tenant.

entries.clue: Time, demonstrating commitment, wants top editor removed (10)

indicators.note: wants = lacks: DEDICATED lacks its top letters ED

blocks.note: an era is a period of time
DEDICATED without the ED (editor) at the top

annotation.surface: A newspaper, showing its resolve, wants its chief editor gone.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface suggests The Times firing its editor; 'wants' means lacks, and the definition is the last word.
annotation.definitionFit: A stronger synonym: eradicated is removed by the roots, from Latin radix, root.

entries.clue: Police almost get man behind bars (7)

indicators.note: almost the whole word: COPS without its last letter

blocks.note: to land a job is to get it

annotation.surface: The police nearly catch the man who ends up in prison.
annotation.walkthrough: The bars are musical bars, not prison bars: Aaron Copland was the American composer behind them.
annotation.definitionFit: Aaron Copland wrote the music, so he is the man behind its bars.

entries.clue: Musical technique in 20th-century song cycles (4)

indicators.note: the first letter goes round to the back

annotation.surface: A composer's device appears in modern song cycles.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Song cycles' looks like a musical term, but 'cycles' is an instruction: SCAT moves its S to the end.
annotation.definitionFit: Cats is Andrew Lloyd Webber's musical.

entries.clue: History exam dealing with life in the country (8)

definitions.text: dealing with life in the country

blocks.note: an oral is a spoken exam

annotation.surface: A history test on rural life.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a school syllabus, so the definition hides as the exam topic.
annotation.definitionFit: Pastoral art or writing deals with country life.

entries.clue: A church service making a simple point? (3)

annotation.surface: A plain church service with a straightforward message.
annotation.walkthrough: The service is a tennis serve: an ace wins the point outright, the simplest point there is.
annotation.definitionFit: An ace is a serve the receiver cannot touch, winning the point at once.

entries.clue: Corrupt party led by deputy (7)

indicators.note: DEP goes in front of RAVE

annotation.surface: A crooked political party headed by the deputy leader.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Corrupt' reads as an adjective about the party, but DEPRAVE is a verb, so it means to corrupt.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, but only as a verb: to lead someone into moral ruin.

entries.clue: Group ready to establish firm (3)

blocks.note: a group of people or things that go together
ready to go, as a runner on the blocks is
to establish or fix a rule or a date
firm as in solid, like a jelly that has hardened

annotation.surface: A group is poised to set up a company.
annotation.walkthrough: There are four definitions here, not two: every word except 'to' is a separate meaning of SET, and 'firm' pretends to be a business.
annotation.definitionFit: A set is a group of people or things that belong together.

entries.clue: Time Out to better The Face? (6,5)

definitions.text: Time Out to better The Face?

blocks.note: the surface wants the London listings magazine; the setter means a break, time off to rest
the surface wants a rival style magazine; the setter means improving your own face

annotation.surface: One magazine, Time Out, is trying to outdo a rival, The Face.
annotation.walkthrough: Time Out (a London listings magazine) and The Face (a style magazine) make it look like a media rivalry; read plainly, it is time off spent improving one's looks.
annotation.definitionFit: Beauty sleep is rest supposed to keep your face looking good.

entries.clue: Feeble quote about pursuing course of action (8)

indicators.note: CITE turned about, back to front
comes after, chasing PATH

blocks.note: a path is a course you take

annotation.surface: A weak quotation is offered about the plan being followed.
annotation.walkthrough: The reversed piece comes second in the answer even though it comes first in the clue, because 'pursuing' puts it behind PATH.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a feeble excuse and a pathetic excuse are the same weak thing.

entries.clue: Child visiting area in work to play (6)

annotation.surface: A child goes to a play area during the working day.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Work to play' sounds like a playground rule, but the work is a musical composition for playing.
annotation.definitionFit: A sonata is a piece of music written for instruments to play.

entries.clue: Peers across at mother’s bottom — it’s out of order! (11)

indicators.note: the letters are not in their proper order

annotation.surface: Aristocrats are shocked at someone's rear end: it's not proper!
annotation.walkthrough: Read 'it's' as 'it is': IT joins the fodder and 'is' links it to 'out of order'.
annotation.definitionFit: Peers are nobles, members of the aristocracy.

entries.clue: Qualification reduced credit for demonstrating negotiating skills (10)

indicators.note: something reduced is made smaller, so the credit word loses its last letter

blocks.note: tick = credit, as in buying on tick, less its K

annotation.surface: A course grants partial credit for showing skill at negotiation.
annotation.walkthrough: Buying on tick is British slang for buying on credit.
annotation.definitionFit: Being diplomatic means handling people with tact, as in negotiation.

entries.clue: Manage to avoid ignominious score in test? (4)

blocks.note: to dodge a duty or a blow, bobbing out of its way
a batsman's score of nought in cricket, named for the egg-shaped zero

annotation.surface: Someone hopes to avoid a shameful mark in an exam.
annotation.walkthrough: The test is a Test match in cricket, where a batsman out for nought has made a duck; the surface wants a school exam.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses of one word: the verb for dodging something and the cricket noun for a batsman's zero.

entries.clue: Make money from openings provided by India’s small enterprises (10)

indicators.note: the opening letters of the next three words

blocks.note: its opening is a capital I, spelt out

annotation.surface: Some business profits from opportunities that small Indian firms supply.
annotation.walkthrough: The trick is that the first letter of 'India's' is a capital, so the answer spells out CAPITAL I before the lower-case s and e.
annotation.definitionFit: The business sense: to turn an asset or opportunity into profit, from capital meaning money invested.

entries.clue: Forbidding relative at home to wear dog’s coat (8)

indicators.note: AUNT IN is worn inside DG
only the outer layer of dog: D and G

blocks.note: first of the outer letters of dog
last of the outer letters of dog

annotation.surface: A stern relative stays in and wears a dog-fur coat.
annotation.walkthrough: The coat is the outside of the word DOG, not its fur.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a forbidding cliff face is one that makes you lose heart before you start.

entries.clue: Detail many works with passion (10)

indicators.note: the letters are worked into a new shape

annotation.surface: Someone lovingly describes a large body of work.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Works' looks like a noun, a list of an artist's works, but it is the verb telling you to rework the letters.
annotation.definitionFit: Doing something animatedly means doing it with liveliness and passion.

entries.clue: Pre-eminent American in charge of antiquities? (7)

annotation.surface: A leading American runs a museum of ancient objects.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the definition is loose: archaic describes very old things.
annotation.definitionFit: Archaic means belonging to an ancient period, like antiquities.

entries.clue: Arrest suspects to populate jails (4)

indicators.note: the answer is locked up inside the neighbouring words

annotation.surface: Police pick up suspects so the prisons fill up.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole surface is about arrests, so 'Arrest' reads as an instruction, not the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Arrest in its older sense of halting something, as in cardiac arrest, not the police sense the surface pushes.

entries.clue: Joint coverage in a report carried by Press Association (7)

indicators.note: PA carries A TELL inside it

annotation.surface: News agency's shared coverage of a story.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Joint coverage' sounds like shared reporting, but the joint is the knee and the coverage its cap. The Press Association is the UK's national news agency.
annotation.definitionFit: The patella is the kneecap, the bone covering the knee joint.

entries.clue: Page provided guidance for one withdrawing guarantee (6)

indicators.note: EG pulls back, reading right to left

annotation.surface: A page gave advice to someone going back on a promise.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Withdrawing guarantee' reads as backing out of a promise; 'withdrawing' works on EG alone and 'guarantee' is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, as either noun or verb: a solemn promise, or something handed over as security.

entries.clue: Managing part of machine storing means of authentication (6)

indicators.note: something storing another thing keeps it inside, so the machine part holds the code

blocks.note: a cog is a toothed wheel in a machine
a PIN proves who you are

annotation.surface: Some machine component holds a security code.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Managing' could be the start of a business phrase; here it means getting by.
annotation.definitionFit: Coping and managing both mean getting by under difficulty.

entries.clue: Understood I’m allowed to embrace power (8)

indicators.note: to embrace is to wrap your arms round, so the outer pieces close round power

annotation.surface: Someone says they understand they are permitted to hold power.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads as someone checking they have permission; 'understood' is the definition in its sense of unspoken but assumed.
annotation.definitionFit: Something implicit is understood without being said.

entries.clue: Provider of notes on staff deserved to lose case (4)

indicators.note: the word's outer letters, its case, are removed

blocks.note: EARNED without its first and last letters

annotation.surface: A staff member who hands out notes deserved to lose a legal case.
annotation.walkthrough: The notes are musical and the staff is the musical stave; Thomas Arne composed Rule, Britannia!
annotation.definitionFit: Arne was a composer, someone who puts notes on the staff.

entries.clue: Publicity surrounding heartless wise man had improved (11)

indicators.note: surrounding means lying all round, so the publicity sits either side of the rest
MELCHIOR loses its central letters CH

blocks.note: Melchior, one of the Three Wise Men, without CH at his heart

annotation.surface: Media attention around a callous sage had made things better.
annotation.walkthrough: Melchior is one of the three Magi in the Nativity story; 'had' is the everyday sense of eating.
annotation.definitionFit: To ameliorate something is to make it better, so ameliorated means improved.

entries.clue: Fish swim, not run (3)

indicators.note: 'not run' means without the run, so that letter is taken away

blocks.note: reel = swim (as a head swims), minus R

annotation.surface: A fish swims but does not run.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Swim' is what your head does when dizzy, so it means reel; r is the cricket abbreviation for a run.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by category: the eel is a long snake-like fish, a crossword regular for its three letters.

entries.clue: Feel bad coverage must be removed from newspaper (3)

indicators.note: the word's outside letters are stripped

blocks.note: DAILY without its outer D and Y

annotation.surface: A newspaper should drop its unpleasant reporting.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Coverage' is press coverage in the surface; in the wordplay it is the cover, the outer letters of DAILY, a daily newspaper.
annotation.definitionFit: A slightly old-fashioned verb for being ill, as in 'what ails you?'

entries.clue: City lent money to auditor introduced by firm (7)

indicators.note: an auditor is a listener, so this is how it is heard
whoever introduces a speaker goes before them, so the firm comes first

blocks.note: money lent is a loan; spoken, it matches the city's second syllable

annotation.surface: A city lent cash to an accountant brought in by a company.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Auditor' is the accountant in the surface but simply a listener in the wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the German city on the Rhine, famous for its cathedral and eau de toilette.

entries.clue: Football team lease empty historic ground (7)

indicators.note: HISTORIC with its contents taken out
ground up, the letters broken down and remixed

annotation.surface: A football club leases an old stadium standing empty.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Ground' is the stadium in the surface and the anagram signal in the wordplay; Chelsea is a London football club.
annotation.definitionFit: Chelsea is an English Premier League football team.
